messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 32-year-old man presents to his primary care provider with right leg weakness and numbness. He reports a 2-day history of “clumsiness” in his right lower extremity after playing in his company’s annual weekend-long charity baseball tournament. He says a similar episode happened 1 year ago during the same tournament. He has a history of major depressive disorder and right distal radius fracture status post-closed reduction and casting after falling 2 years ago. He takes fluoxetine. He also reports that he several years ago he had an isolated episode of decreased vision and inability to move his right eye that resolved on its own. He has a 15-pack-year smoking history and drinks 3-4 beers per week. His temperature is 98.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 115/65 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, and respirations are 18/min. On exam, hip flexion, knee extension, and ankle dorsiflexion are all 3/5 on his right and 5/5 on his left. Right Achilles and patellar reflexes are 1+ on the right and 2+ on the left. He has decreased sensation to light touch throughout the right leg especially below the knee. Additional questioning would most likely reveal which of the following additional features about this patient’s current symptoms?

Options:
A. Concomitant hyperreflexia
B. Symptom improvement in the heat
C. Symptom exacerbation in the heat
D. Symptom exacerbation with repetitive muscle contractions
E. Symptom improvement with repetitive muscle contractions

Correct answer: C. Symptom exacerbation in the heat

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This is a neurology question about multiple sclerosis and Uhthoff phenomenon; the depression and fluoxetine details are incidental distractors."}
